newsitem.title: UK: Latin American origins prevail on sugar freight mk.
newsitem.headline: Latin American origins prevail on sugar freight mk.

text.p: Latin American origins dominated activity on the sugar freight market on Tuesday to a variety of end destinations, shipbrokers said.
Cuba was again a popular origin for bulk raws into European destinations.
Vitol quoted for a spot 14,000-tonne cargo of bulk sugar from Cuba to Klaipeda with options of Casablanca, Egyptian Med and Black Sea.
Pacol fixed 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from the same origin to the Black Sea for mid-February at a rate though to be in the low $30 bracket.

Louis Dreyfus was open for 14/15,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Colombo for 17/21 February and was believed to have fixed 21,000 tonnes from the same origin to US Gulf for end-February.

Shipbrokers said Sugar Chartering was in the market for 25/29,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic for February/March and CSR quoted for 17,000 tonnes from Queensland to Japan for March dates.
In other news, London traders said Iran bought at least two cargoes of raw sugar at its recent tender and probably one cargo of white sugar as well.
The raws were thought to be Cuban in origin and were bought for March 15/April 15 shipment.
